data.title: Oil-Dri outlines $375M total borrowing capacity while signaling potential reinvestment above prior ~$35M capex pace
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Oil-Dri Corporation of America (ODC) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "We've never been more happy or positive with how the company is doing." (Chairman, CEO & President Daniel Jaffee)
  • "We did give some forward guidance back in the first quarter and second quarter. We said the first part of F'26 was going to be a tough comparison, but that we fully expected to equal or more than make up the distance in the back half." (Chairman, CEO & President Daniel Jaffee)
  • "You see the really great fourth quarter we had, which allowed us to do just that, pull ahead in many key indices, sales, net income, things like that, EBITDA, all were up for the fiscal year." (Chairman, CEO & President Daniel Jaffee)
  • "Oil-Dri delivers record annual financial results, including all-time high fourth quarter sales and historic cash generation." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Susan Kreh)
  • "Our cash position, together with our ability to access debt, provides strong liquidity and gives us flexibility to fund strategic priorities, manage through volatility, and pursue attractive growth opportunities while maintaining a very disciplined balance sheet." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)

Outlook

  • "Our capital priorities remain unchanged from what we have told you previously." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "First, we will continue to invest in our business." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "Second, we will continue to support our dividend." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "Third, we will evaluate opportunities to achieve long-term profitable growth through the pursuit of strategic acquisitions." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "Finally, we opportunistically evaluate potential value creation through share repurchases." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)

Financial Results

  • "That fourth quarter growth was broad-based across both product groups, with business-to-business sales rising 4% to a record $50 million, and retail and wholesale increasing 3% to $79 million." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "Gross profit as a percent of sales or, gross margin, was under pressure and remained steady at 27.8%." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "Cash and cash equivalents reached an historic high of $74 million at year end, up from $51 million a year ago, marking a significant 45% increase." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "We generated operating cash flow of $80 million and EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, of $93 million." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "We extended our variable rate revolving credit facility and increased our borrowing capacity by 33%, up to $100 million." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "At the same time, we extended our fixed rate shelf facility and increased our borrowing capacity by 100%, up to $150 million." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)
  • "So in total, we have increased our ability to borrow under these two facilities from $200 million to $375 million." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh)

Q&A

  • "Was there a seasonal factor in Amlan's last quarter?" (Ethan Star: Question) "The fourth quarter was, again, exceptional. That's a rate we probably can't maintain. But we should see very good growth year-over-year as we continue to expand our Amlan business." (Vice President of Agriculture Wade Robey: Answer)
  • "Fluids Purification sales declined 5% for the full year, but delivered their strongest quarterly performance in the fourth quarter. What drove the improvement in Q4 compared to the rest of fiscal year '26?" (Robert Smith and John Bair: Question) "The decline in sales did not reflect customer losses. It was just variation in demand." (Chairman, CEO & President Jaffee: Answer)
  • "Walk us through the capacity and customer concentration dynamics" (Tyler Ventura, Diamond Hill Capital: Question) "We are obligated under contracts with our co-man customers to not disclose a ton about the nature of those relationships." (Group Vice President of Business to Business & Strategic Growth Initiatives Christopher Lamson: Answer)
  • "Could you please discuss the challenges and opportunities you see in growing your branded cat litter distribution and sales?" (Ethan Star: Question) "Some of the challenges we've seen in the past year for our branded cat litter distribution are increasing slotting costs, customer investment requirements, and other spend requirements that are rising faster than the pricing -- than our pricing and inflation." (VP & GM of Consumer Products Division Laura Scheland: Answer)
  • "What is structurally driving this growth?" (Leslie Garber: Question) "We saw over 95 million acres of corn planted in the U.S. this past season, about 85 million of soy." (Vice President of Agriculture Robey: Answer)
  • "With the expanded revolver and the removal of the $100 million acquisition cap, how should we think about the size and focus of acquisitions you're considering" (Jens Verbrugge, Value Square Funds: Question) "We are very disciplined around being mission-led, around value -- creating value with sorbent minerals." (Group Vice President Lamson: Answer) "So it is possible that you could see some bigger reinvestment in the business at levels higher than you've seen in the past." (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh: Answer)

Sentiment Analysis

  • "The reason I ask is because your domestic clay litter sales are actually declining" (Tyler Ventura, Diamond Hill Capital: Question) and "Any guidance on balance sheet and the usage of a bit of financial leverage would be helpful." (Jens Verbrugge, Value Square Funds: Question) reflected a slightly negative to neutral analyst tone focused on mix, potential cannibalization, concentration, and leverage boundaries.
  • "We've never been more happy or positive with how the company is doing." (Chairman, CEO & President Jaffee) and "we're very bullish on the growth going forward" (Vice President Robey) reflected positive management sentiment; in Q&A, management was more guarded on disclosure, saying "we are obligated under contracts... to not disclose a ton" (Group Vice President Lamson).
  • "We had also indicated that we expected to pick up year-over-year momentum in the second half of our fiscal year" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh, Q3) aligned with Q4’s message that "the focus team here at Oil-Dri delivered on that forecast" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh, Q4), indicating consistent confidence quarter to quarter.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • "Our gross margin... was unfavorably impacted by a 190 basis point reduction" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh, Q3) contrasted with Q4 where "gross margin... remained steady at 27.8%" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh, Q4), while cost pressures persisted, including "higher freight and transportation expenses" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh, Q4).
  • Q3 emphasized operations and reinvestment-driven margin pressure, including "the margins are going to continue to get pressured" (Chairman, CEO & President Jaffee, Q3), while Q4 emphasized balance sheet capacity, including "increased our ability to borrow... from $200 million to $375 million" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh, Q4).
  • Analyst focus shifted from Q3 category demand and biofuels exposure to Q4 questions centered on co-packaged cat litter dynamics and acquisition capacity, including "capacity and customer concentration dynamics" (Tyler Ventura, Diamond Hill Capital, Q4) and "the expanded revolver" (Jens Verbrugge, Value Square Funds, Q4).

Risks and Concerns

  • "Our gross per ton domestic cost of goods sold increased 3% over the same quarter in the prior year, primarily due to higher freight and transportation expenses" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh) and "reduced capacity in the trucking industry" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh) were cited as ongoing cost risks.
  • "This pressure was especially impactful in the Retail and Wholesale Products Group" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh) where freight costs on cat litter contributed to "a 5% decline in segment operating income" (CFO & Chief Information Officer Kreh).
  • "Volumes varied as changes in oil type and feedstock quality impacted customers' needs" (Chairman, CEO & President Jaffee) described volatility risk in Fluids Purification demand even as management said "the decline in sales did not reflect customer losses" (Chairman, CEO & President Jaffee).

Final Takeaway

Oil-Dri management framed fiscal 2026 as a year where a tougher first-half comparison was followed by a stronger second half, and highlighted record full-year sales and net income alongside what it called "historic cash generation." Management emphasized that freight and transportation costs pressured results in parts of the portfolio, while also pointing to an expanded financing toolkit—raising total borrowing capacity to $375 million—to preserve flexibility for continued reinvestment, dividends, and potential acquisitions, with selective disclosure limits around key co-packaging relationships.

data.title: Microsoft's Nadella unveils tech giant's new fast decision-making AI model
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) CEO Satya Nadella on Friday unveiled the company's new fast decision-making artificial intelligence model, Microsoft-Decision-1.

“It delivers top performance on structured decision tasks, outperforming both LLMs and other decision models in latency and quality,” Nadella wrote in a post on X. “We’re already testing it across Microsoft for everything from incident response and quality control to scientific discovery.”

“This model is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control, making it easier to incorporate decision intelligence into existing applications, agents, and workflows in a secure, trusted environment. Microsoft-Decision-1 delivers top performance in latency and quality on structured decision tasks to outperform both LLMs and other decision models,” Microsoft wrote in a blog post.

Microsoft-Decision-1  is 4.5 times quicker than Quyet-1.0-Large and 35 times quicker than OpenAI's (OPENAI) GPT-6 Sol, Microsoft added.

Pricing for the new model is $0.42 per 1M tokens for input tokens, while output tokens are free.

The new model is available in Microsoft Foundry and will soon be available in OpenRouter, Microsoft added.

GSK to expand Pennsylvania presence with over $800M investment
data.description:
• GSK (GSK) will expand its already substantial presence in Pennsylvania with a more than $800M investment to boost operations in Montgomery County.
  • As a result, ~300 jobs will be added over the next five years. The pharma already employs ~4500 full-time employees in the state.
  • The expansion, which will begin next year in Upper Merion Township, will include knocking down current buildings and constructing new ones, including a commercial-scale biologics manufacturing facility. In addition, a R&D pilot plant will be established, as well as a centralized quality control lab and manufacturing science and technology hub. 
  • GSK's latest investment in the Keystone State follows an October 2024 announcement of an up to $800M investment to boost R&D and manufacturing at a facility in Lancaster County.

data.title: Wall Street advances as tech pain eases
data.description:
Wall Street regained some momentum on Friday, after the AI trade came under pressure on Thursday.

S&P 500 (SP500) +0.6%, the Dow (DJI) +0.9%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +0.6%. 

10 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors were in the green, led by real estate and health care as the top gainers, while communication services was the only loser.

Tech shares came under pressure on Thursday amid revenue concerns surrounding OpenAI (OPENAI). Reports indicated that OpenAI's annualized revenue reached $50B at the end of September, below the $68B figure reported the previous month.

"But it looks as if the initial knee-jerk reaction has been tempered to some degree, possibly as an insider explained that the $68 billion figure included gross revenues from partners," said Trade Nation analyst David Morrison. "Nevertheless, investors will bear in mind that OpenAI has delayed the IPO previously expected this year."

On the economic front, consumer sentiment fell more than expected in October's initial reading as inflation expectations accelerated.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 5 basis points to 4.81%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 2 basis points to 5.26%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) rose 1 basis point to 5.62%.

data.title: S&P 500 flatline masks historic churn across individual stocks - Nomura
data.description:
While the headline S&P 500 index (SPY) (VOO) appears placid on the surface, underlying individual stocks are experiencing wild volatility reminiscent of a full-blown crisis, according to Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott.

The S&P 500 moved just 0.8% over the past month, while the average constituent stock swung by 8.9%, McElligott wrote in a recent note. This 8.1 percentage point dispersion gap ranks in the 95th percentile of historical data over the past 30 years, reflecting an extraordinary level of churn beneath a deceptively quiet benchmark.

McElligott stressed that far from being complacent, the market is undergoing a substantial “rolling correction” driven by rising interest rate pressures and severe capital displacement toward artificial intelligence. Over the trailing 30 days, Technology, Media, and Telecommunication, or TMT, and Energy (XLE) were the only S&P 500 sectors to post positive returns, while rate-sensitive sectors took a heavy beating—led by real estate investment trusts (XLRE) (-9.8%), materials (XLB) (-7.9%), and financials (XLF) (-7.7%).

Damage across individual constituents is widespread: 85% of S&P 500 stocks were down more than 10% from their all-time highs, and 59% were in deep bear-market territory, down over 20%, the strategist noted. The benchmark's stability is almost single-handedly anchored by a tiny cluster of mega-cap AI leaders, with just ten stocks—led by Nvidia (NVDA), Micron (MU), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), and AMD (AMD)—accounting for 70% of the market's 23% rally since late March.

data.title: Hedge funds cut Bitcoin, brokerages load up in Q2: CoinShares report
data.description:
Professional investors increased their Bitcoin (BTC-USD) holdings in second-quarter, even as overall U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holdings declined, according to a CoinShares report published Friday.

13F filers held 264K BTC at the end of June, up 1.3% from 261K tokens in the first-quarter. Meanwhile, total U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holdings fell 6.3%, and non-13F holders reduced their exposure by 8.3%.

The dollar value of 13F filers’ holdings fell 13% to $15.5B as Bitcoin’s price declined 14% during the quarter. However, their share of total U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF AUM rose to 22.4% from 20.8%, marking the first increase since second-quarter 2025. 

Hedge funds cut exposure as brokerages buy

Hedge funds recorded the largest reduction, cutting their Bitcoin exposure by 10.8K coins (22%) to 37.8K BTC.

DE Shaw exited its 3.7K BTC position, while Millennium Management reduced its holdings from 14.4K BTC to 7.3K BTC.

Investment advisors also trimmed exposure, reducing holdings by 4.6K BTC, or 3%, to 145.7K BTC. Brevan Howard cut its position by 9.6K BTC to 4.1K BTC.

The advisors nevertheless accounted for roughly 55% of all reported 13F Bitcoin holdings.

At the same time, brokerage holdings more than doubled to 38.5K BTC from 17K BTC. Jane Street added 10.9K BTC to reach 16.9K BTC, while Morgan Stanley (MS) held 10.4K BTC. However, Morgan Stanley’s Q1 filing was excluded from the earlier comparison, partly affecting the increase.

Bank of Montreal (BMO) and VanEck Associates each added roughly 2.6K BTC.

Other notable sellers included Avenir Tech, which reduced its position by 2.8K BTC, SIG Holding, which cut 2.4K BTC, and IMC-Chicago, which reduced its holdings by 2.3K BTC.

Government and university endowment holdings remained broadly unchanged, while private-equity exposure rose 5% to 6.9K BTC.

Now, the third-quarter filings will show whether brokerage buying continues and whether professional investors maintain their Bitcoin exposure following the second-quarter decline.
